answer: A lagoon stays healthy only when fresh water flows in from many streams, and an agent economy can work the same way: require each identity to build a diverse web of reciprocal interactions with many independent counterparties, like boats docking at a busy wharf instead of circling one pier. Sybil clusters reveal themselves because their internal links are dense while links to the wider economy are sparse, the graph's pigment showing one flat color instead of varied hues. Forging that diversity costs an attacker sustained, genuine-looking engagement with real agents, which scales poorly.
